The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: Switching off a setting moved the shop's account pages onto newer code that likely breaks for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, because it tries to work out an average over zero purchases.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 12m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 35.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 7,533.46 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #560 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while legacy-checkout-fallback was off
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 04:29 to 04:41 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 8 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 05:08:57 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 04:35:57 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 04:29 UTC and was back to normal at 04:41 UTC, 12 minutes later. 29.3% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 35.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 7,533.46 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching off a setting moved the shop's account pages onto newer code that likely breaks for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, because it tries to work out an average over zero purchases. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help; reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #560, for a person to review and merge. If legacy-checkout-fallback is turned off again, account pages could go back onto the new renderer and fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.

Impact
12m 0s - onset until back to normal
35.5% - peak error rate
4,224 - requests failed
1.0% to 29.3% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
7,533.46 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
In the files Code-Fix read, the new renderer's monthly spend summary (`average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, line 47) divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases it made this month, and nothing guards against that count being zero. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError, and `serve_account_page` catches the error and returns a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed: the service's own account-page error-rate warning rose from its usual level, and the error-rate alert fired.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 10 occurrences in 10 minutes, 04:26–04:35; # was 1.00% to 33.00%, typically 26.50%, highest at 04:35
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
why 1 Account page requests were raising ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py from the onset minute (04:29–04:35 UTC), and the account page handler turned each one into a failed page.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 04:29–04:35
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
why 2 Account pages had moved from the legacy renderer to the new renderer, whose spend summary runs the line that raised. The legacy renderer's count was highest at 04:26 UTC and the new renderer's at 04:30 UTC.
  Evidence:
    Gc27d INFO io-shop: account pages served - # by the legacy renderer, # by the new renderer - 10 occurrences in 10 minutes, 04:26–04:35; # was 0 to 200, typically 0, highest at 04:26; # was 0 to 200, typically 200, highest at 04:30
    F1
why 3 The legacy-checkout-fallback flag was switched off at 04:29:13 UTC. Flag evaluations went from all on before the onset to mostly off in the onset minute, and then to all off.
  Evidence:
    P1 04:29:13 UTC flag toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
    G153f INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=on - 200 evaluations - 3 occurrences in 3 minutes, 04:26–04:28
    G7ad6 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 152 / on 48 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 04:29
    G7037 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 04:30–04:35
  Ruled out:
    The monthly-spend-feature flag, switched on at the same instant (04:29:13 UTC): turning it off left the service at the incident's level, and the service came back with it still on once legacy-checkout-fallback was turned back on.
      T17 04:37:30 Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
      T19 04:39:11 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - still at the incident's level
      T20 04:40:20 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON
      T22 04:40:30 Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2, moved from OFF to ON
      T24 04:42:14 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 04:41
      T25 04:42:14 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 04:30; the Investigator Agent read back 2 production changes.
      T7
      T8
why 4 The new renderer's spend summary divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month, and Code-Fix's reading of the source says that number is zero for an ordinary shopper who has not bought this month.
  Evidence:
    F1
    G5309
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that tested the new renderer's spend summary with an account that has past purchases but none this month before a flag could send production account pages to it. Code-Fix's reading says the test file's own fixture calls such a shopper the ordinary case. (AI-3)
- Switching off legacy-checkout-fallback took most flag evaluations off within the onset minute and all of them from the next minute, which sent all account page traffic to the new renderer. No staged rollout of the flag change to a small share of traffic was seen. (AI-4, AI-5)
- Two flags on the same service were changed by the same actor at the same instant, so the investigation could not tell from the record which one caused the errors. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | At 04:29:13 UTC the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on, enabling the spend summary path. It raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and fails about 30% of account page requests. No deployment or code change was involved. | 0.55 | refuted
C2 | At 04:29:13 UTC the legacy-checkout-fallback flag was switched off. Account pages moved from the legacy renderer to the new renderer, and the new renderer's spend summary raises ZeroDivisionError. | 0.40 | confirmed

Trigger
legacy-checkout-fallback flag went from ON to OFF at 04:29:13 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 04:37:30 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
M2 | 04:40:30 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 04:43:55 | Proposed a fix: PR #560 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 04:29 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 04:35:34 UTC, 6 minutes 34 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #560 | open
AI-3 | Before a feature flag on io-shop can send production traffic onto a new code path, require that path's tests to pass against ordinary account data, including an account with past purchases but none this month. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Roll out io-shop feature flag changes to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only after the error rate holds. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Stop a staged flag rollout on io-shop automatically and revert it when the service's error rate rises during the rollout. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Change feature flags on io-shop one at a time, with an observation window between changes. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop so that it pages the on-call engineer. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-8 | Keep legacy-checkout-fallback on until the fix under review in AI-2 is merged and deployed, and record that hold where flag owners will see it. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 1 minute 42 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 04:29.
- 1 minute 56 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 4 minutes 46 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON.
- 4 minutes 56 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2, moved from OFF to ON.
- 8 minutes 21 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #560.
What went wrong
- The person's lead in the thread named the right flag before the investigation began, but the investigation ranked that flag second. The first revert went to the wrong flag, and the right one waited until that revert was judged.
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault is in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, in average_spend_per_item_this_month: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month) (line 47, the line the investigation's errors point to). The divisor is the number of purchases this account made in the current month. A shopper who has bought before but not this month makes that zero, and that is an ordinary shopper: the test file's own fixture calls this "the ordinary case". Each request that render_spend_summary sends down the monthly path (use_monthly_summary=True) for such a shopper raises ZeroDivisionError. serve_account_page in src/io_shop/account_page.py catches it and returns a failed page. Turning the legacy-checkout-fallback flag off sent more account pages down this new path. That exposed the fault; the flag did not cause it. With the code as it stands, the flag cannot safely be turned off again.

The fix: when there are no purchases this month, the function returns 0, meaning no spend this month, and does not divide. Shoppers who did buy this month take the same path as before. The lifetime average and its deliberate ZeroDivisionError for an account with no history at all are unchanged, so the existing boundary tests that rely on that error still hold. The line-number test also still holds, because it goes through the lifetime function, whose lines this change does not move. No error is swallowed: the guard checks the one known empty case and returns a defined figure for it.

The new tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py cover a shopper with past purchases and none this month. They call the function directly and also through render_spend_summary with use_monthly_summary=True, and assert 0. Against the current code both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist

✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)

○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, account pages on io-shop failed to load for some shoppers. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. Turning off a setting moved the account pages onto newer code. That code likely breaks for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, because it tries to work out an average over zero purchases. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus first reverted the monthly-spend-feature flag, but that did not help, so Argus put it back. Argus then reverted the legacy-checkout-fallback flag. That change was confirmed to help and is still in place. Argus has also opened a proposed fix to the code as a draft.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
